notes.okusoma: The ku- form is the infinitive: “to …”.

guidebook.intro: With a handful of verbs and the subject prefixes, you can describe a whole day. The verb stem stays the same; only the front changes.

tips.title: Who is doing it
body: You know **n-** (I) and **o-** (you). Add **a-** (he or she), **tu-** (we), **mu-** (you all) and **ba-** (they). Lusoga has no separate word for he and she.
The **ku-** form is the infinitive, “to …”: **okusoma** (to read), **okukola** (to work). Use it after **Njagala**: **Njagala okusoma**, I want to read.

culture.title: Three meals
body: **Ekyenkya** (breakfast) is often tea with bread or a snack, **ekyemisana** (lunch) is the main meal for many, and **ekyegulo** (supper) is eaten after dark. Each name comes from the time of day.
